facts.text: FluidLab is a set of standardized complex robotic fluid manipulation tasks powered by FluidEngine, a multi-material fully differentiable physics engine supporting liquids, solids and gases
Every environment is registered as <env_name>-v<id> with entry point fluidlab.envs.<env_name.lower()>_env:<EnvName>Env, kwargs version and loss_type='default', and max_episode_steps=10000
CirculationEnv requires the version argument and takes loss=True, loss_type='diff' and seed=None
CirculationEnv has horizon 1000 and horizon_action 1000
With loss_type='default' gym_misc replaces the horizon with horizon_action
The action range of the circulation environment is [-0.1, 0.1]
The circulation agent has 8 action dimensions
The action velocity scales are 1 for the first six dimensions, 100000 for dimension seven and 50 for dimension eight
The environment is a 3-D Taichi MPM simulation with particle density 1e6, 100 local substeps, gravity (0, -20, 0), horizon 1000 and CPU checkpoints
The scene adds a room static mesh at position (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), euler (0, 0, 0), scale (1.4, 3.0, 1.4), SDF resolution 128, material PILLAR and dynamics enabled
The scene adds one 'nowhere' body of 10 water particles
The smoke field is resolved at 128, with dt 0.03, 50 solver iterations, decay 0.99 and q_dim 1
The observation samples at most 200 particles per body
gym_misc builds observation_space as Box(-inf, inf, obs.shape) and action_space as Box(action_range[0], action_range[1], (agent.action_dim,))
reset restores the stored initial state and returns the observation
_get_obs concatenates each body's sampled positions, velocities and used flags, the agent state, and the smoke field's v and q slices taken as [::10, 60:68, ::10]
step clips the action to action_range before advancing the simulator
The episode ends when t equals horizon; a NaN reward is replaced with -1000 and also ends the episode
seed calls the base environment's seed and then sets the process random seeds
The step reward of the circulation loss is 11 minus the current step loss
The air-conditioner effector's get_state output is a 9-element vector: position (3), quaternion (4), strength s and radius r
The MPM physics timestep is 2e-4 s and one environment step covers int(2e-3 / self.dt) substeps

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 records the seed, and reset restores the stored initial state of the environment, so the same seed and the same actions repeat a trajectory; this package's fake is deterministic and does not draw a random state at reset, and upstream draws scene particles with numpy at construction time

gaps: the upstream model is a multi-material differentiable MPM fluid and smoke simulation; the fake integrates a small agent-only state and models no particles, smoke, contacts or fluid forces

the fake observation is a 9-value agent-state slice (position, quaternion, strength s and radius r); for this scene the upstream observation concatenates 5487 float32 values: 70 body state (10 particles of x, v and used), 9 agent state, 4056 smoke v samples and 1352 smoke q samples

one cap.world.step.v1 tick is one environment step; the MPM simulator runs int(2e-3 / 2e-4) internal substeps of 2e-4 s per step, so the control period is 2e-3 s (timestep_ms 2.0) and the substeps are not individually addressable through the bridge
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time only by the declared step
no actuator, sensor or noise model: the AirCon scales are applied to the simplified agent state, and the reward is a stand-in, not the 11 minus temperature-loss formula of the upstream loss
the fake uses Python floats and lists; upstream returns float32 numpy arrays from a Taichi simulation and its scene is built with numpy's random generator
snapshot and restore are not offered: FluidEnv exposes no get_state/set_state through the environment object the bridge inspects
no physical device is modelled and neither the model nor the fake was compared with the upstream environment or validated against any device

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
